title: Will the Foot Strike Pattern Change at Different Running Speeds with or without Wearing Shoes?
publisher: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
claims: Twenty healthy male regular runners ran on a treadmill from slow to fast paces, with and without shoes, in random order; foot strike was recorded with a high-speed camera.
Foot strike pattern was significantly correlated with shoe condition (chi-square = 99.07, p < 0.01); the authors describe correlation, not causation.
When running with shoes, runners preferred a heel strike regardless of running speed; 95% used rearfoot strike at initial, slow and fast speeds, reduced by only 5% at the ultimate speed.
When running barefoot, only 23.8% of landings were rearfoot, and the distribution of strike patterns did not change significantly with speed (chi-square = 2.26, p = 0.89).
The authors conclude that foot strike preference is correlated with footwear condition rather than running speed.
